findings.finding: The web-session grant epoch is taken from the request body (`GrantObservation.declared_epoch = self.body.key_epoch`, web_session/mod.rs:768) and passed through the checked `grant_facts`/`plan_grant` as the epoch to grant (vela-session-policy/src/lib.rs:205-217, 99-121). The verified policy only requires `declared_epoch >= INITIAL_EPOCH`; the tie to the live account epoch is the SQL CAS `EXISTS (... users ... key_epoch = ?)` in `StoreStmt::GrantWebSession` (vela-session-policy/src/store.rs:2461-2470), not a proved observation. Functionally a stale or forged epoch fails the CAS, but the value used as authentication context is request-supplied. `GrantObservation.mode` is also body-chosen (`web_session/mod.rs:761`); the policy admits ReadWrite only with a stored `web_vk` (`lib.rs:99-121`), so that value stays a bounded request parameter. O13c should derive the epoch from a store read observation or prove the CAS guard as the binding.

Every recovery-share mutation takes its epoch from the request (`body.key_epoch` at recovery/mod.rs:271,407; `X-Vela-Epoch` header at recovery/mod.rs:637) and then calls `recovery_mutation_permit(epoch)` (recovery/mod.rs:42-55) with the same value as both `declared_epoch` and `authority_epoch`. The resulting `ShareRequestObservation.device_authority` is therefore a constant `true` (recovery/mod.rs:275,409,539,655) rather than an observation. The only real binding is the SQL predicate `WHERE id = ? AND key_epoch = ? AND rekey_state IS NULL ...` (vela-recovery-policy/src/share_store.rs:264-277). The possession path has the same shape: the attempt envelope is written with the request's `user_id` and generated `recovery_id` (`recovery/possess.rs:271-274,152`) and the recovery driver later compares the consumed envelope's user/attempt with the request (`possession_store.rs:211`), so the binding is a compare over body-chosen ids, not an authenticated identity. This is the recovery counterpart of O1-F1 and belongs to O13e.

`POST /auth/verify` (login) builds the device identity and verifier context from the request body: `device_id_str = body.device_id.to_string()` (auth/verify.rs:321), the device row is looked up by that id (auth/verify.rs:123), and the same string is passed into `verify_auth_signature` (auth/verify.rs:175). Login is unauthenticated by design, so this is expected; it is recorded here because the driver's `DeviceObservation` and `VerifierObservation` are decided over a body-chosen identity plus an open verifier verdict, and O13c must not mistake the row read for a session-derived context.

Share-EK registration uses the body timestamp `signed_at` for the monotonic freshness relation (`vela_share_policy::timestamp_is_fresher(self.canonical_signed_at, current_since)`, share/mod.rs:972-975) after a canonical-form and 300 s future-skew check (share/mod.rs:1038-1046). The value is covered by the device signature over `share_ek_binding_message(share_ek, signed_at)` (share/mod.rs:942-944), and the stored `share_ek_since` cell is a proved row read, so the producer is not an unauthenticated context; O13a should still record that the compared instant is body-supplied (signed) rather than clock- or row-derived.

The pairing claim uses the request body's `hybrid_ek`/`hybrid_vk`; the verified claim policy observes only their decoded lengths (`ClaimObservation.hybrid_ek_len/hybrid_vk_len`, vela-enrollment-policy/src/lib.rs:106-118; rendezvous.rs:284-301). The completion path then reads the *stored* claim and verifies the opener's signature over it (`claim_key_source: StoredClaim`, lib.rs:271-293; rendezvous.rs:620-676,732-750), so enrollment authority is not body-derived. The claim's key material itself is body-supplied and length-checked only (1600/2624 bytes); users compare it out of band. Also, the redemption path records `hybrid_ek_len`/`hybrid_vk_len` from the request body (recovery/enroll_device.rs:341-342) after exact decoded-length checks. O13d should state the trust chain explicitly.

The middleware's first admission call passes `account_present: true` and `device_row_active: true` as placeholders (middleware.rs:116-124) because neither can matter while a revocation marker is set; the tail is re-evaluated with real reads at middleware.rs:143-149 and 181-188. The pure `admission_is_authorized` proof is unaffected, but the observation-honesty claim for those two fields holds only at the later call sites. O13d/O13c should treat the first call as a partial observation.

Actor observations are constants at every call site: `ActorObservation { authenticated: true, device_active: true }` (device/revoke.rs:207-210), `DeletionActorObservation` (account/delete.rs:212-216), `ShareActorObservation`/`actor()` (recovery/mod.rs:65-71), `GrantActorObservation` (web_session/mod.rs:843-846), `DeleteActorObservation` (web_session/mod.rs:1443-1446). Their truth rests entirely on the `DeviceSession`/`AuthSession` extractor and its PASETO verification, which are open (08: token issuance and verifier inputs; middleware admission is a pure decision). This is the single largest open origin across the areas.

Freshness values come from the OS: challenge nonces `getrandom::getrandom` (auth/challenge.rs:183, recovery/possess.rs:247), and identifiers from `Uuid::new_v4()` (e.g. share/mod.rs:355 inbox id, recovery/enroll_device.rs:354 device id, recovery/possess.rs:152 attempt id). The policies observe only lengths/freshness booleans; entropy quality and v4 uniqueness are open (plan O11/T9).

Clock reads feed observations directly: `Utc::now()` into `SendRequestObservation`-adjacent values and expiry (`send.rs:191,291`, `share/mod.rs:356`), web-session `TokenSessionObservation.now` (web_session/mod.rs:996), grant expiry (web_session/mod.rs:769), recovery-share timeout `TimeoutFacts.expired` (vault/rekey.rs:147-152), and TTL-based key lifetimes. 08 lists TTL expiry as a scheduler choice; O9 must model expiry as adversarial deletion rather than trust the clock.

`SendObservation.recipient_has_share_ek` is a literal `true` in the driver (vela-share-policy/src/driver.rs:664), set after `SendAdmissionObservation.recipient_can_receive` passed (driver.rs:647). The verified fact is therefore not independently observed at that point; the real producer is the recipient probe (share/mod.rs:157-166, store.rs:856). Not a bug, but the inventory records the indirection so a later refinement does not over-credit the fact.
